name: Jaddai
title: One of those who sent away their foreign wives
summary: Jaddai was one of the Israelites who had taken foreign (non-Jewish) wives during the period after the exile in Babylon. He is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of those who agreed to send away their foreign wives to obey God's law and cleanse the people from mixed marriages.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among those who had taken foreign wives
keyEvents.description: Jaddai is mentioned in the list of Israelites who had married women from foreign nations, which was contrary to God's law.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's reform movement
keyEvents.description: Under Ezra's leadership, the people were gathered to address the issue of mixed marriages. Jaddai was among those affected by this reform.

keyEvents.title: The people's confession and pledge
keyEvents.description: The people confessed their sin and pledged to send away their foreign wives in obedience to God's word, a commitment that Jaddai also made.

keyEvents.title: Investigation of the matter
keyEvents.description: A commission was established to investigate all cases of mixed marriages. Jaddai's case was handled as part of this process.
